terms.title: Closure
terms.definition: A closure gives you access to an outer function's scope from an inner function.
terms.explanation: In JavaScript, closures are created every time a function is created, at function creation time.
terms.example: function outer(){ let x=10; return function(){ return x; } }

terms.title: Scope
terms.definition: The current context of execution in which values and expressions are visible or can be referenced.
terms.explanation: JavaScript has global scope, module scope, function scope, and block scope.
terms.example: if (true) { let x = 5; } // x is block-scoped

terms.title: Hoisting
terms.definition: The process where variable and function declarations are moved to the top of their scope before code execution.
terms.explanation: Var declarations are hoisted as undefined, while let/const declarations are hoisted into a Temporal Dead Zone.

terms.title: Let Keyword
terms.definition: Declares a block-scoped local variable, optionally initializing it to a value.
terms.explanation: Can be reassigned but cannot be re-declared within the same scope.

terms.title: Const Keyword
terms.definition: Declares block-scoped read-only constants.
terms.explanation: The value of a const variable cannot be reassigned, though mutable objects held in const can still be modified.

terms.title: Var Keyword
terms.definition: Declares a function-scoped or globally-scoped variable.
terms.explanation: Legacy variable declaration method; lacks block scoping and is subject to hoisting behaviors.
terms.example: var x = 10; var x = 20; // Allowed with var

terms.title: Promise
terms.definition: An object representing the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation.
terms.explanation: Can exist in one of three states: pending, fulfilled, or rejected.

terms.title: Async / Await
terms.definition: Syntactic sugar built on top of Promises to write asynchronous code synchronously.
terms.explanation: The async keyword transforms a function into a promise returner; await pauses execution until the promise settles.
terms.example: async function fetchData() { const res = await fetch('/url'); }

terms.title: Callback Function
terms.definition: A function passed into another function as an argument to be invoked later.
terms.explanation: Often used for asynchronous actions or array iteration methods.

terms.title: Fetch API
terms.definition: A modern web standard interface for fetching resources asynchronously across the network.
terms.explanation: Returns a Promise that resolves to the Response object representing the response to the request.

terms.title: Event Loop
terms.definition: The mechanism that allows JavaScript to perform non-blocking I/O operations despite being single-threaded.
terms.explanation: Continuously checks the Call Stack and moves tasks from the Task Queue/Microtask Queue to the stack when empty.

terms.title: Call Stack
terms.definition: A LIFO (Last In, First Out) data structure used by the JS engine to keep track of function execution.
terms.explanation: When a function is called, it's pushed onto the stack. When it finishes, it's popped off.
terms.example: function a(){ b(); } function b(){ return 1; } a();

terms.title: Task Queue
terms.definition: A queue holding callbacks from asynchronous browser APIs (like setTimeout or DOM events).
terms.explanation: Also called the Macrotask Queue, processed by the Event Loop after the Microtask Queue is emptied.
terms.example: setTimeout(callback, 0) // Enqueues task into Macrotask Queue

terms.title: Microtask Queue
terms.definition: A high-priority queue reserved for callbacks originating from promises, queueMicrotask, and MutationObserver.
terms.explanation: Processed completely before the Event Loop moves to the next Macrotask.

terms.title: Arrow Function
terms.definition: A compact alternative to a traditional function expression with lexical binding of 'this'.
terms.explanation: Arrow functions cannot be used as constructors and do not have their own arguments object.

terms.title: This Keyword
terms.definition: Refers to the context in which the current function is executed.
terms.explanation: Value depends on how the function was called (global, method invocation, call/apply/bind, or new).

terms.title: Prototypes
terms.definition: The mechanism by which JavaScript objects inherit features from one another.
terms.explanation: Every object has an internal link to another object called its prototype.

terms.title: Prototype Chain
terms.definition: The chain of linked prototype objects used to resolve property and method lookups.
terms.explanation: Property lookup walks up the prototype chain until the property is found or null is reached.

terms.title: Bind Method
terms.definition: Creates a new function that, when called, has its 'this' keyword set to the provided value.
terms.explanation: Unlike call or apply, bind returns a new function without immediately executing it.

terms.title: Classes
terms.definition: Syntactic sugar over JavaScript's existing prototype-based inheritance model.
terms.explanation: Provides clearer syntax for object creation, constructors, methods, and static methods.

terms.title: Call and Apply
terms.definition: Methods used to invoke a function immediately with an explicit 'this' context.
terms.explanation: call() takes arguments individually, while apply() accepts arguments as an array.

terms.title: Destructuring
terms.definition: Syntax that allows unpacking values from arrays or properties from objects into distinct variables.
terms.explanation: Drastically reduces boilerplate code when extracting data.
terms.example: const { name, age } = user; const [first, second] = list;

terms.title: Spread Operator
terms.definition: Allows an iterable like an array or object to be expanded in places where zero or more arguments/elements are expected.
terms.explanation: Represented by three dots (...) to expand array elements or clone objects.

terms.title: Rest Parameters
terms.definition: Allows a function to accept an indefinite number of arguments as an array.
terms.explanation: Uses the three dots (...) syntax as the last parameter in a function signature.
terms.example: function sum(...numbers) { return numbers.reduce((a, b) => a + b); }

terms.title: Array Map
terms.definition: Creates a new array populated with the results of calling a provided function on every element.
terms.explanation: Does not mutate the original array; returns a new array of identical length.

terms.title: Array Filter
terms.definition: Creates a shallow copy of a portion of a given array, filtered down to elements that pass a test condition.
terms.explanation: Elements that evaluate to true in the callback function are kept.

terms.title: Array Reduce
terms.definition: Executes a user-supplied 'reducer' callback function on each element of the array, passing in the return value from the calculation on the preceding element.
terms.explanation: Reduces an entire array down to a single output value (number, object, array, etc.).

terms.title: Event Bubbling
terms.definition: A type of event propagation where the event first triggers on the innermost target element, and then triggers on ancestors.
terms.explanation: Travels upwards from target to window unless stopped with stopPropagation().

terms.title: Event Delegation
terms.definition: A pattern where you attach a single event listener to a parent element to manage events for all its children.
terms.explanation: Relies on event bubbling to catch events on dynamically created child nodes.

terms.title: DOM Manipulation
terms.definition: The interaction with the Document Object Model tree to dynamically change page structure, style, or content.
terms.explanation: Utilizes native methods like querySelector, createElement, and appendChild.

terms.title: Debounce
terms.definition: A programming practice used to ensure that time-consuming tasks do not fire so often.
terms.explanation: Delays executing a function until after a specific amount of time has elapsed since its last invocation.
terms.example: Used for search input auto-complete fields to prevent excessive API calls.

terms.title: Throttle
terms.definition: A technique that limits the maximum number of times a function can be called over time.
terms.explanation: Guarantees function execution at regular time intervals during ongoing user events (e.g., scrolling).
terms.example: Used on window resize or scroll handlers.

terms.title: Currying
terms.definition: A technique of evaluating a function with multiple arguments into a sequence of functions with single arguments.
terms.explanation: f(a, b, c) is transformed into f(a)(b)(c).
terms.example: const multiply = a => b => a * b; const double = multiply(2);

terms.title: Strict Mode
terms.definition: A way to opt in to a restricted variant of JavaScript.
terms.explanation: Eliminates some JS silent errors by changing them to throw explicit errors, enhancing performance/security.
terms.example: 'use strict'; x = 3.14; // Throws error because x is un-declared

terms.title: Optional Chaining
terms.definition: Operator that enables reading the value of a property located deep within a chain of connected objects without validation.
terms.explanation: Represented by ?. symbol; short-circuits to return undefined if reference is nullish.

terms.title: Nullish Coalescing
terms.definition: A logical operator (??) that returns its right-hand side operand when its left-hand side operand is null or undefined.
terms.explanation: Unlike logical OR (||), nullish coalescing does not fall back on falsy values like 0 or empty strings.

terms.title: Generators
terms.definition: Functions that can be exited and later re-entered, preserving context and variable bindings across re-entries.
terms.explanation: Declared using function* syntax and utilize the 'yield' operator.

terms.title: Iterators
terms.definition: An object which defines a sequence and a return value upon its termination via a next() method.
terms.explanation: Must implement a next() method returning an object with { value, done } properties.

terms.title: Symbols
terms.definition: A primitive data type whose instances are unique and immutable.
terms.explanation: Primarily used as unique identifiers for object properties to avoid property name collisions.

terms.title: Map Object
terms.definition: A keyed collection holding key-value pairs where any value (objects/primitives) can be used as either a key or a value.
terms.explanation: Remembers insertion order and maintains size property natively unlike plain Objects.

terms.title: Set Object
terms.definition: A collection of unique values of any type.
terms.explanation: Automatically deduplicates entries; common method for removing array duplicates.

terms.title: WeakMap and WeakSet
terms.definition: Collections of key/value pairs or values in which keys/values must be objects and are held weakly.
terms.explanation: Garbage collector can clean up keys if no other references exist, preventing memory leaks.

terms.title: Garbage Collection
terms.definition: Automatic memory management process that reclaims memory occupied by objects no longer reachable.
terms.explanation: Modern JS engines use mark-and-sweep algorithms to handle memory reclamation.
terms.example: Setting an object variable to null marks previous reference for collection.

terms.title: Proxy
terms.definition: An object that wraps another object and intercepts operations like reading, writing properties, and function calls.
terms.explanation: Enables custom behavior traps for fundamental operations (get, set, deleteProperty).
terms.example: const p = new Proxy(target, { get: (t, prop) => t[prop] ?? 'Default' });

terms.title: Reflect API
terms.definition: A built-in object that provides methods for interceptable JavaScript operations.
terms.explanation: Mirror object of Proxy traps, providing cleaner functional methods to manipulate objects.

terms.title: ES Modules
terms.definition: The official standardized module system for JavaScript.
terms.explanation: Uses import and export directives to share code between isolated files.
terms.example: import { useState } from 'react'; export default Component;

terms.title: CommonJS
terms.definition: A module standard used primarily in Node.js applications.
terms.explanation: Uses module.exports and require() syntax; executes synchronously.

terms.title: Web Workers
terms.definition: A feature allowing scripts to run in background threads, detached from the main execution thread.
terms.explanation: Enables execution of heavy computation without freezing or lagging the user interface.

terms.title: LocalStorage and SessionStorage
terms.definition: Web storage APIs allowing key/value pairs to be saved in the web browser.
terms.explanation: LocalStorage persists across sessions, while SessionStorage clears when the tab closes.

terms.title: Type Coercion
terms.definition: The automatic or implicit conversion of values from one data type to another.
terms.explanation: Can cause unexpected results when using abstract equality (==) instead of strict equality (===).
